implementation.name: GNU Bison in its Yacc-compatible C workflow
implementation.version_scope: Bison manual and generator source checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: Yacc-style grammars describe syntax and semantic actions for generated parsers; this profile selects GNU Bison.

prerequisites.text: Learn grammar rules, tokens and a lexer/parser interface; this C workflow also needs a C compiler.

execution.text: Bison generates C parser source, which is compiled with the supplied lexer and driver.

behavior.text: yyparse consumes tokens from yylex and executes actions when grammar rules reduce.

tooling.text: Bison provides conflict diagnostics and parser tracing; a lexer can be handwritten or generated separately.

maintenance.text: Keep grammar, lexer, generator version and chosen skeleton together to reproduce parser behavior.

costs.text: The generator is GPL-3.0-or-later; the manual explains a separate generated-parser exception whose applicability is visible in output notices.

example.run_instructions: Generate with bison -o marker.c marker.y, compile with cc marker.c -o marker, and run marker with input p followed by a newline and end-of-input.
example.expected_result: Accepts that input and prints accepted; other characters cause a parser error.

implementation.name: solc standalone Yul compiler, EVM dialect
implementation.version_scope: Solidity 0.8.38-develop Yul documentation checked on 2026-10-13; no latest stable-version claim.

sources.label: Yul syntax, EVM dialect and standalone compilation

fit.text: Yul is compiler intermediate code and a standalone low-level EVM language; it also appears in Solidity inline assembly.

prerequisites.text: Learn EVM values, memory, storage and return-data conventions before relying on low-level code.

execution.text: solc --strict-assembly compiles standalone Yul; a separate EVM host executes the emitted bytecode.

behavior.text: Built-ins such as add, mstore and return operate on EVM values and memory; they do not provide console printing.

tooling.text: The command-line compiler and standard-JSON interface accept Yul, with explicit optimizer and EVM-target settings.

maintenance.text: The manual describes active development and fully implemented bytecode generation for the EVM dialect; pin compiler and target settings.

costs.text: The compiler's GPL text is separate from Yul program licensing and any host or network execution costs.

example.run_instructions: Compile locally with solc --strict-assembly --bin total.yul. To inspect the return value, execute that code in a local EVM harness; no public deployment is required.
example.expected_result: Compilation emits EVM bytecode. Executing this code returns a 32-byte word encoding 5; it is a return-data demonstration, not a persistent callable deployed contract.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.

implementation.name: Zeek scripting engine
implementation.version_scope: Book of Zeek 9.0.0 scripting documentation checked on 2026-10-13.

sources.label: Zeek scripting events and data types

fit.text: Zeek scripts react to analysis events and shape network logs and detections within the Zeek host.

prerequisites.text: Learn event handlers and native address, subnet and port types; packet analysis additionally needs an appropriate input source.

execution.text: The host invokes startup and protocol handlers; this small script runs in bare mode without packet input.

behavior.text: Queued events run subsequently rather than returning values like immediate function calls.

tooling.text: ZeekControl manages deployment configuration, while BTest supports focused script and trace-based tests.

maintenance.text: Keep scripts matched to the Zeek event APIs and deployed configuration; handler ordering can use explicit priorities.

costs.text: Zeek's implementation uses BSD-3-Clause; separately loaded packages and deployment services retain their own terms.

example.run_instructions: With Zeek installed, run zeek -b port.zeek in an empty working directory.
example.expected_result: Prints the port value 443/tcp at startup without requiring a traffic capture.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: Retain the required notices and disclaimer; the source license does not cover every external Zeek package.

implementation.name: Zig 0.15.2 compiler
implementation.version_scope: Zig 0.15.2 language reference and tagged license; installation guidance checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: Zig compiles typed programs and provides low-level control, compile-time expressions and C integration.

prerequisites.text: Install the selected Zig bundle; learn explicit types, optionals, errors and allocator ownership when allocating memory.

execution.text: zig build-exe compiles an executable; projects can instead use the generated build.zig workflow.

behavior.text: Compile-time evaluation and runtime checks have different rules; undefined does not initialize a meaningful value.

tooling.text: The compiler supports tests and build commands, and the getting-started guide links editor integration through ZLS.

maintenance.text: Use documentation for the exact compiler version; the project distinguishes tagged releases from development builds.

costs.text: The selected compiler uses MIT; bundled third-party code and linked C libraries require their own notices.

example.run_instructions: Using Zig 0.15.2, run zig build-exe total.zig, then run the generated total executable.
example.expected_result: Displays 5 through the standard library's debug output.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: The tagged compiler license grants MIT for covered files; bundled dependencies and target runtime components may differ.
